title: Spring beans and component scanning

richText: A bean is a Java object that Spring creates or accepts and then manages.
The application context is Spring’s container for these beans and their configuration.
creates this context during application startup.
Spring needs a bean definition before it can create a bean. The definition tells it which class or factory method to use.
call creates a Java object. It does not register that object with Spring.
This lesson covers registration. The next lesson explains how one bean receives another bean.
Component scanning searches configured packages for classes carrying Spring component annotations.
makes a class a candidate for this search.

Spring registers a definition for each discovered component. It normally creates these singleton beans during startup.
Discovery does not call the class’s application methods.

richText: A bean’s scope determines how Spring shares its instances.
The default singleton scope keeps one instance per bean definition in one application context.
Several classes receiving that bean normally share the same object.
Singleton scope does not make mutable fields thread-safe.
The lifecycle lesson covers creation and shutdown after dependency injection has been introduced.
